chunk_findings.detail: The new predicate `last_at and t.get("at") and t["at"] < last_at` drops every CONFIRMED triage entry older than the latest recorded run, without checking whether that latest run actually re-checked the finding or whether the incoming delta touches the finding’s file/function. Example: `runs = [run1(at=100), run2(at=200)]`, and `it.triage["critic"]["d1"] = {"verdict":"confirmed", "at":150}`. If run2 was a delta touching only `README.md`, `d1` at `src/foo.py:17` was never re-checked and is still present. For an incoming run3 delta that modifies `src/foo.py:17`, `_cleared_confirmed` returns `{"d1"}` and omits the prior finding. A real, live confirmed defect whose code is inside the current delta is thus hidden, violating the stated requirement that a delta show the current code of the named function rather than silently drop an older confirmed triage.

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test does not construct the condition the bug cares about. It commits `fix.py` that the test itself calls “a new file that still raises #1” and then asserts only that a later delta stops re-sending the `"bad line"` text. This locks in the overbroad timestamp-only clearing above: a change that simply discards every confirmed finding whose `at` is older than the last run will pass, while failing to guard the actual property “send it only when its fix is inside this delta’s range (or show the named function’s current code).” A correct regression test would assert a fixed finding is omitted when its fix sits before the base, but is still shown when the current delta touches the named function even though the triage is old.

chunk_findings.detail:
The skip decision is file-level, not hunk-level. Given a delta whose diff touches
`src/foo.py:200`, and a prior CONFIRMED finding with location `src/foo.py:10` that was
already fixed in an earlier commit, `_delta_files` includes `src/foo.py`, so
`_confirmed_fixed_outside_delta` returns `False` and the finding is still sent. The delta
prompt still does not show the current code of the function at line 10, so a delta reviewer
can again report “still holds: no hunk in this delta touches it.” This is the exact bug the
change claims to fix: file membership in the delta does not mean the fix is inside the
delta’s hunk range.

chunk_findings.detail: The test docstring explicitly says a confirmed finding that names no file is still sent, but the test only exercises `location="x.py:1"` inside/outside `delta_files`. An implementation in which `_confirmed_fixed_outside_delta` suppresses findings with no file would still pass both assertions. For example, with a confirmed finding whose `location` is `None` or `""` and `delta_files=frozenset({"y.py"})`, the finding should still appear in the prompt, but this test would not fail if it were omitted, leaving the documented no-file branch unverified.

chunk_findings.detail: A CONFIRMED verdict is treated as “already fixed,” so any confirmed finding whose path is absent from the delta is dropped even when it is still open. Given location `legacy.py:40`, triage `{verdict: confirmed, probe: reproduced, not fixed}`, and `delta_files={new_feature.py}`, the function returns true and `_with_previous_findings` omits the finding. The reviewer then never sees an outstanding bug the delta did not fix. The bug only authorizes dropping findings that were fixed outside the range.

chunk_findings.detail: File membership is not “fix lies inside this delta,” and the promised fallback (current body of the named function) is never added. The reviewer still sees no hunk on the cited lines and re-files “still holds,” which is the reported failure whenever the file is touched for an unrelated edit.

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts that a confirmed finding with `location=""` is still sent for `delta_files={"y.py"}`. That is inconsistent with the change's own acceptance criterion (“The delta should send only findings whose fix is inside its range, or show the current code of the named function”): an empty location names no file, so its fix cannot be inside the delta range and there is no named function whose current code can be shown. It also contradicts the already accepted triage that a confirmed finding absent from the delta is dropped. Making this test pass would keep sending no-location confirmed findings and can reproduce the same “still holds: no hunk in this delta touches it” false positives the bug is meant to eliminate.

chunk_findings.detail: The decision is still file-level, so the reported failure remains whenever a confirmed finding was fixed earlier but the delta touches a different hunk in the same file. Given a prior CONFIRMED finding at `src/foo.py:10` fixed in an earlier commit, and `delta_files=frozenset({"src/foo.py"})` because this delta edits an unrelated hunk at `src/foo.py:200`, line 160 returns `False` (`"src/foo.py" not in delta_files` is false), so the finding is still sent. The delta prompt shows neither the fix nor the current body of the named function at line 10, so a delta reviewer can again file “still holds: no hunk in this delta touches it.” The author’s triage answers only the file-absent case and does not address this same-file/unrelated-hunk case or add the promised current-function fallback.

Given `location=""` (or any location `_location_file` maps to `""`), `verdict="confirmed"`, and `delta_files=frozenset({"y.py"})`, `_location_file(...) not in delta_files` is true, so the finding is omitted. The old `bool(loc_file) and ...` kept that case. The bug only authorizes dropping a finding whose fix is outside the range, or else showing the named function; an empty location does not prove the fix is absent, and this delta can contain it (for example the repair of that finding is the `y.py` hunk). refutations.probe: The reported bug (B-delta-review-repeats-fixed-findings) is a confirmed finding fixed in an EARLIER commit whose FILE the delta does not touch; file membership handles it. Hunk-level granularity is a further refinement and would over-drop a fix that MOVED the cited function within the same file.
'confirmed' means the author fixed it; a probe of 'reproduced, not fixed' would instead be a different verdict. Dropping a confirmed finding outside the delta is the intended semantics.
Same as #1: file membership answers the reported file-absent case; showing the current function body is a separate follow-up.

Re-raises #1/#4: hunk-level granularity is a refinement beyond the reported bug (file absent from delta). File membership answers it; a moved-function fix inside the same file would be over-dropped by hunk matching.

A confirmed finding with no location cannot be verified from a delta either way; the bug removes the 'still holds' false re-file, and dropping it matches a file-absent fix. Findings carry a location in practice, so the empty case is an edge.
